transformations.edit: Replaced the seed string recorder with an executable Verus function for the Rust 1.96 target body.

Adapted the inherent mutable `[T]` receiver to an explicit `slice_ref: &mut &mut [T]` parameter, removed `const`, and named the return value for Verus; no target-body path was externalized or assumed.

Lowered unsupported `mem::replace(self, &mut [])` to the lifetime-preserving executable swap-with-empty sequence `let mut replacement = &mut []; core::mem::swap(slice_ref, &mut replacement); let slice = replacement;`, which preserves the old inner mutable slice for the following split.

Lowered the following `split_first_mut` empty/nonempty behavior to `slice.len() != 0`, `slice.split_at_mut(1)`, and `&mut head[0]`, preserving the first/rem data flow before executing `*slice_ref = rem` and `Some(first)`.

Added proof-only `lemma_split_at` and view equality assertions to connect the swap-lowered first/rem views to `slice_split_off_first_result`, the final slice reference, and the returned mutable element length composition.
